decisions.choice: makes a special vow: a vow out of the ordinary
decisions.reason: The verb means to do something remarkable or beyond the usual. With "vow" it describes a solemn, uncommon promise, here the promise of a person to the LORD. The same phrase opens the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6:2). A vow was a promise to give God something, often in return for help asked of him (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11).

decisions.choice: your valuation of persons: the fixed price of a person, paid in silver
decisions.reason: The word means an assessment or set value. Its ending "your" is fixed in this formula through the whole chapter and is never explained; it may once have addressed Moses or the priest, but it works as a technical term, "the valuation". The person vowed (oneself or a member of the household) was not handed over to the sanctuary; the vow was kept by paying the value set out in verses 3-7. Hannah's gift of Samuel to serve at the sanctuary (1 Samuel 1:11, 28) shows the other way such a vow could be kept.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone who vows, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the law covers anyone who makes such a vow; Numbers 30 deals with the vows of women. The valuations that follow are set by the sex and age of the person vowed, not of the one who makes the vow.

decisions.choice: the value of a person / the set price
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the fixed "your", which in this phrase names no particular person, and say what the valuation is. Literal keeps "your valuation" through the chapter.

decisions.choice: Then they are to pay the set price for that person.
decisions.reason: Readable states outright what verse 3 implies: the person vowed is released by paying the value that follows. Literal and Balanced leave the sentence open into verse 3.

decisions.choice: "tu valoración" (L); "la valoración", "el valor" (B); "el precio fijado" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter. Literal keeps the fixed "your" of the Hebrew formula, as "según tu valoración" in 5:15; Balanced drops it, as the English does; Readable says what it is, a set price.

decisions.choice: "alguien", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English puts "a person|a man" under the gender setting through this chapter. Spanish "alguien" already means anyone, man or woman (m3), so the Spanish needs no span here or in verses 14, 16, 26, 28 and 31.

decisions.choice: "ton estimation" (L); "l'estimation", "la valeur" (B); "le prix fixé" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter. Literal keeps the fixed "your" of the Hebrew formula, as "selon ton estimation" in 5:15; Balanced drops it, as the English does; Readable says what it is, a set price.

decisions.choice: "quelqu'un", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English puts "a person|a man" under the gender setting through this chapter. French "quelqu'un" already means anyone, man or woman (m3), and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French (docs/french-style.md section 7), so the French needs no span here or in verses 14, 16, 26, 28 and 31.

decisions.choice: "makadirio yako" (L); "thamani" (B); "bei iliyowekwa" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter. The formula recurs in nearly every verse, so Literal uses the noun "makadirio" (assessment) with the fixed "your" instead of the relative clause of 5:15, which grows heavy when repeated; Balanced says "thamani" (value) and Readable "bei iliyowekwa" (the set price).

decisions.choice: "서원" for the vow (Readable "약속"); "네가 매기는 값" (Literal), "사람의 값" (Balanced), "정해진 값" (Readable) for the valuation
decisions.reason: "서원" is the term sheet's word for a vow; Readable says "약속" as the English Readable says "promise". The valuation is a fixed price in silver, which "값" says without the sense of ransom that "몸값" carries.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה עֶרְכְּךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר מִבֶּן֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֗ חֲמִשִּׁ֛ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כֶּ֖סֶף בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be your valuation of the male from a son of twenty year[s] and to a son of sixty year[s], and will be your valuation fifty shekel[s] of silver by [the] shekel of the holy place.

en.B: the valuation for a man from twenty to sixty years of age is to be fifty shekels of silver, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
en.R: For a man between twenty and sixty years old, the set price is fifty shekels of silver, weighed by the official shekel used at the holy tent.

es.R: Por un hombre de entre veinte y sesenta años, el precio fijado es de cincuenta siclos de plata, pesados con el siclo oficial que se usaba en la tienda santa.

ko.L: 남자는 스무 살부터 예순 살까지이면, 네가 매기는 값은, 곧 네가 매기는 값은 성소의 세겔로 은 오십 세겔이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 스무 살부터 예순 살까지의 남자는 성소의 세겔로 달아 은 오십 세겔로 값을 매긴다.

decisions.choice: shekels of silver: a weight of silver, not a coin
decisions.reason: The shekel was a unit of weight, about 11.5 grams or two-fifths of an ounce. Coins were not yet in use; silver was weighed out (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9-10). Fifty shekels was about 20 ounces of silver. For comparison, the law sets thirty shekels as the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32), and fifty shekels is the sum paid in Deuteronomy 22:29.

decisions.choice: by the shekel of the holy place: by the standard sanctuary weight
decisions.reason: Weights could differ from place to place. "The shekel of the holy place" was the official standard used for payments to the sanctuary, fixed at twenty gerahs (verse 25; Exodus 30:13), as in 5:15.

decisions.choice: the male from twenty to sixty: the first of four age groups
decisions.reason: The values in verses 3-7 are set by sex and by age: twenty to sixty, five to twenty, one month to five years, and over sixty. Twenty is the age at which men were counted for the army and paid the half shekel (Exodus 30:14; Numbers 1:3). The text does not explain how the amounts were fixed; they are the prices for releasing a vow, not a measure of a person's worth before God.

decisions.choice: shall be — your valuation shall be
decisions.reason: The Hebrew starts the sentence, breaks off after the age range, and starts again with "your valuation shall be". Literal shows the restart with a dash; Balanced and Readable say it once.

decisions.choice: measured by
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "measured" to make clear that the sanctuary shekel is the standard weight for the payment. Readable says "weighed by".

decisions.choice: "para el sexo masculino" ... "para el sexo femenino" (verses 3-7)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are "male" and "female", which the English Literal keeps. Spanish "macho" and "hembra" are said of animals and would sound demeaning of people, so Literal says "of the male / female sex". Balanced and Readable say man, woman, boy, girl, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "pour le sexe masculin" ... "pour le sexe féminin" (verses 3-7)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are "male" and "female", which the English Literal keeps. French "femelle" is said only of animals and would be insulting of a woman, so Literal says "of the male / female sex" for both. Balanced and Readable say homme, femme, garçon, fille, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "세겔" kept as a unit with no units span; "성소의 세겔" (Literal, Balanced), "성막에서 쓰는 공식 세겔" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The English gives these prices in shekels with no metric span, since they are fixed prices rather than weights to picture; the Korean follows it. Readable explains the sanctuary shekel as the English Readable does.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [mtu ni] tangu umri wa mwezi mmoja hadi umri wa miaka mitano, ndipo makadirio yako ya mtu wa kiume yatakuwa shekeli tano za fedha, na ya mtu wa kike makadirio yako [yatakuwa] shekeli tatu za fedha.
sw.B: Kwa mtoto wa mwezi mmoja hadi miaka mitano, thamani ni shekeli tano za fedha kwa mtoto wa kiume na shekeli tatu za fedha kwa mtoto wa kike.
sw.R: Kwa mtoto mwenye umri wa kati ya mwezi mmoja na miaka mitano, bei iliyowekwa ni shekeli tano za fedha kwa mvulana na shekeli tatu za fedha kwa msichana.

ko.L: 그리고 한 달부터 다섯 살까지이면, 네가 매기는 값은 남자는 은 오 세겔, 여자는 네가 매기는 값이 은 삼 세겔이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 태어난 지 한 달부터 다섯 살까지의 아이는 남자는 은 오 세겔, 여자는 은 삼 세겔로 값을 매긴다.
ko.R: 태어난 지 한 달부터 다섯 살까지의 아이는 남자아이는 은 오 세겔, 여자아이는 은 삼 세겔이 정해진 값이다.

decisions.choice: from a month: from the age of one month
decisions.reason: A child younger than a month was not counted; the firstborn son was redeemed at one month for five shekels (Numbers 3:15; 18:16), the same amount set here for a boy.

source.text: וְ֠אִם מִבֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה וָמַ֨עְלָה֙ אִם־זָכָ֔ר וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֔ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר שָׁ֑קֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֥ה שְׁקָלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And if from a son of sixty year[s] and upward, if [a] male, and will be your valuation fifteen shekel[s], and for the female ten shekels.

en.L: And if [the person is] from sixty years old and upward, if a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
en.B: For someone sixty years old or more, the valuation is fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman.
en.R: For a person over sixty years old, the set price is fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman.

es.L: Y si [la persona es] de sesenta años para arriba, si es del sexo masculino, entonces tu valoración será de quince siclos, y para el sexo femenino diez siclos.
es.B: Por alguien de sesenta años o más, la valoración es de quince siclos para un hombre y de diez siclos para una mujer.
es.R: Por una persona de más de sesenta años, el precio fijado es de quince siclos por un hombre y diez siclos por una mujer.

fr.L: Et si [la personne a] soixante ans et au-delà, si c’est le sexe masculin, alors ton estimation sera de quinze sicles, et pour le sexe féminin de dix sicles.
fr.B: Pour quelqu’un de soixante ans ou plus, l’estimation est de quinze sicles pour un homme et de dix sicles pour une femme.
fr.R: Pour une personne de plus de soixante ans, le prix fixé est de quinze sicles pour un homme et de dix sicles pour une femme.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [mtu ni] tangu umri wa miaka sitini na kuendelea, ikiwa ni wa kiume, ndipo makadirio yako yatakuwa shekeli kumi na tano, na ya mtu wa kike shekeli kumi.
sw.B: Kwa mtu wa miaka sitini au zaidi, thamani ni shekeli kumi na tano kwa mwanamume na shekeli kumi kwa mwanamke.
sw.R: Kwa mtu mwenye umri wa zaidi ya miaka sitini, bei iliyowekwa ni shekeli kumi na tano kwa mwanamume na shekeli kumi kwa mwanamke.

ko.L: 그리고 예순 살 이상이면, 남자일 경우 네가 매기는 값은 십오 세겔, 여자는 십 세겔이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 예순 살이 넘은 사람은 남자는 십오 세겔, 여자는 십 세겔로 값을 매긴다.
ko.R: 예순 살이 넘은 사람은 남자는 십오 세겔, 여자는 십 세겔이 정해진 값이다.

decisions.choice: from sixty upward: the oldest age group
decisions.reason: The values fall for those over sixty, more for men (from fifty to fifteen shekels) than for women (from thirty to ten).

source.text: וְאִם־מָ֥ךְ הוּא֙ מֵֽעֶרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְהֶֽעֱמִידוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֶעֱרִ֥יךְ אֹת֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן עַל־פִּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר תַּשִּׂיג֙ יַ֣ד הַנֹּדֵ֔ר יַעֲרִיכֶ֖נּוּ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And if [too] poor he [is] for your valuation, and he will station him before the priest, and will value him the priest; according to the mouth of what will reach [the] hand of the one vowing will value him the priest.

en.L: But if he is too poor for your valuation, then he shall set him before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to what the hand of the one who vowed can reach, the priest shall value him.
en.B: But if the one who vows is too poor to pay the valuation, the person is to be brought before the priest, and the priest will set a value for them, fixing the amount by what the one who vowed is able to pay.
en.R: But someone may be too poor to pay the set price. Then the person who was promised must be brought to the priest. The priest will decide on a price that the one who made the promise is able to pay.

es.L: Pero si él es demasiado pobre para tu valoración, entonces lo presentará delante del sacerdote, y el sacerdote lo valorará; conforme a lo que alcance la mano del que hizo el voto, lo valorará el sacerdote.
es.B: Pero si el que hace el voto es demasiado pobre para pagar la valoración, la persona será presentada ante el sacerdote, y el sacerdote le fijará un valor, de acuerdo con lo que pueda pagar el que hizo el voto.
es.R: Pero puede ser que alguien sea demasiado pobre para pagar el precio fijado. Entonces la persona prometida tiene que ser llevada al sacerdote. El sacerdote decidirá un precio que pueda pagar el que hizo la promesa.

fr.L: Mais s’il est trop pauvre pour ton estimation, alors il le placera devant le prêtre, et le prêtre l’estimera ; selon ce que peut atteindre la main de celui qui a fait le vœu, le prêtre l’estimera.
fr.B: Mais si celui qui a fait le vœu est trop pauvre pour payer l’estimation, la personne sera présentée au prêtre, et le prêtre fixera sa valeur, d’après ce que celui qui a fait le vœu a les moyens de payer.
fr.R: Mais il peut arriver que quelqu’un soit trop pauvre pour payer le prix fixé. Alors la personne promise doit être amenée au prêtre. Le prêtre décidera d’un prix que celui qui a fait la promesse peut payer.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa yeye ni maskini mno kwa makadirio yako, ndipo atamsimamisha mbele ya kuhani, naye kuhani atamkadiria thamani; kulingana na kile ambacho mkono wa yule aliyeweka nadhiri unaweza kufikia, kuhani atamkadiria.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa aliyeweka nadhiri ni maskini mno kuweza kulipa thamani hiyo, mtu huyo atalazimika kuletwa mbele ya kuhani, naye kuhani atamkadiria thamani kulingana na kile ambacho aliyeweka nadhiri anaweza kulipa.
sw.R: Lakini huenda mtu akawa maskini mno kuweza kulipa bei iliyowekwa. Hapo lazima mtu aliyeahidiwa aletwe kwa kuhani. Kuhani ataamua bei ambayo yule aliyetoa ahadi anaweza kulipa.

ko.L: 그러나 만일 그가 가난하여 네가 매기는 값을 [낼 수] 없으면, 그는 그 사람을 제사장 앞에 세우고, 제사장이 그의 값을 매길 것이다. 서원한 사람의 손이 미치는 만큼에 따라 제사장이 그의 값을 매겨야 한다.
ko.B: 그러나 서원한 사람이 너무 가난하여 정한 값을 낼 수 없으면, 서원한 대상인 사람을 제사장 앞에 데려가야 한다. 그러면 제사장이 서원한 사람의 형편에 맞게 값을 정해 줄 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 어떤 사람은 너무 가난해서 정해진 값을 낼 수 없을 것이다. 그러면 바치기로 약속한 사람을 제사장에게 데려가야 한다. 제사장은 약속한 사람이 낼 수 있는 만큼 값을 정해 줄 것이다.

decisions.choice: he ... him: the one who vowed brings the person vowed
decisions.reason: "He" who is too poor is the one who made the vow. "Him" whom he sets before the priest is most likely the person vowed, who may be the vower himself. The verb "set" is literally "make stand", to present someone formally.

decisions.choice: what the hand can reach: what the person can afford
decisions.reason: "His hand reaches" means he has the means for something, as in 5:7, 11; 14:21-22, 30-32 for the poor who bring smaller offerings. The vow is not cancelled but scaled to the vower's means.

decisions.choice: the one who vows / the person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant by each "he" and "him", following m1. Literal keeps the pronouns.

source.text: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֥ן מִמֶּ֛נּוּ לַיהוָ֖ה יִֽהְיֶה־קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if an animal which people bring near of it [as] an offering to Yahweh, all that he gives of it to Yahweh will be holy.

en.L: And if [it is] an animal of which [people] bring near an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all that he gives of it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall be holy.
en.B: If the vow is of an animal of the kind that may be presented as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, any such animal given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} becomes holy.
en.R: Someone may promise an animal of a kind that can be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Any animal given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in this way becomes holy.

es.L: Y si [es] un animal del que [se] presenta ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, todo lo que uno dé de él {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} será santo.
es.B: Si el voto es de un animal de los que se pueden presentar como ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, todo animal así dado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} queda santo.
es.R: Alguien puede prometer un animal de los que se pueden ofrecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Todo animal dado así {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} se vuelve santo.

fr.L: Et si [c’est] un animal dont [on] fait approcher une offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, tout ce qu’on en donnera {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} sera saint.
fr.B: Si le vœu porte sur un animal de ceux qu’on peut présenter en offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, tout animal ainsi donné {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} devient saint.
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut promettre un animal d’une espèce qu’on peut offrir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Tout animal donné de cette façon {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} devient saint.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [ni] mnyama ambaye [watu] humsogeza kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kila atakachotoa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika hao kitakuwa kitakatifu.
sw.B: Ikiwa nadhiri ni ya mnyama wa aina inayoweza kutolewa kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kila mnyama wa namna hiyo aliyetolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakuwa mtakatifu.
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kuahidi mnyama wa aina inayoweza kutolewa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kila mnyama aliyetolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa njia hii anakuwa mtakatifu.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 [그것이] 사람들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 가까이 바치는 짐승이면, 그 가운데서 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 드리는 것은 모두 거룩할 것이다.
ko.B: 서원한 것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 바칠 수 있는 짐승이면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 드린 그 짐승은 모두 거룩하게 된다.
ko.R: 누가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 바칠 수 있는 짐승을 바치겠다고 약속할 수 있다. 그렇게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 드린 짐승은 모두 거룩하게 된다.

decisions.choice: an animal that may be brought as an offering: a clean animal fit for the altar
decisions.reason: Cattle, sheep and goats could be offered (1:2); unclean animals could not (verse 11). An offering here is the general word for what is brought near to the LORD, as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: will be holy: it now belongs to the LORD and cannot be taken back
decisions.reason: Once vowed, the animal belongs to the LORD and must be offered. Unlike the animals of verses 11-13, it cannot be redeemed; the next verse forbids even exchanging it.

source.text: לֹ֣א יַחֲלִיפֶ֗נּוּ וְלֹֽא־יָמִ֥יר אֹת֛וֹ ט֥וֹב בְּרָ֖ע אוֹ־רַ֣ע בְּט֑וֹב וְאִם־הָמֵ֨ר יָמִ֤יר בְּהֵמָה֙ בִּבְהֵמָ֔ה וְהָֽיָה־ה֥וּא וּתְמוּרָת֖וֹ יִֽהְיֶה־קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not he will replace it and not he will exchange it, good for bad or bad for good; and if indeed he exchanges an animal for an animal, and will be it and its substitute holy.

en.L: He shall not replace it and shall not exchange it, a good for a bad or a bad for a good; and if he does indeed exchange animal for animal, then it and its substitute shall be holy.
en.B: The owner must not swap it or put another in its place, a good animal for a poor one or a poor one for a good one. If they do replace one animal with another, both the first animal and the one put in its place will be holy.
en.R: The owner must not trade it for another animal, a better one for a worse one or a worse one for a better one. If they do trade, then both animals will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: No lo sustituirá ni lo cambiará, uno bueno por uno malo, o uno malo por uno bueno; y si de hecho cambia un animal por otro animal, entonces él y su sustituto serán santos.
es.B: El dueño no debe cambiarlo ni poner otro en su lugar, uno bueno por uno malo o uno malo por uno bueno. Si llega a reemplazar un animal por otro, tanto el primer animal como el que puso en su lugar serán santos.
es.R: El dueño no debe cambiarlo por otro animal, ni uno mejor por uno peor ni uno peor por uno mejor. Si lo cambia, los dos animales serán {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Il ne le remplacera pas et ne l’échangera pas, un bon contre un mauvais ou un mauvais contre un bon ; et s’il échange vraiment un animal contre un animal, alors lui et son remplaçant seront saints.
fr.B: Le propriétaire ne devra pas le changer ni en mettre un autre à sa place, un bon pour un mauvais ou un mauvais pour un bon. S’il remplace malgré tout un animal par un autre, le premier animal et celui qu’il a mis à sa place seront saints tous les deux.
fr.R: Le propriétaire ne doit pas l’échanger contre un autre animal, ni un meilleur contre un moins bon, ni un moins bon contre un meilleur. S’il fait l’échange, les deux animaux appartiendront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Hatambadilisha wala hatambadili, mzuri kwa mbaya au mbaya kwa mzuri; na kama kweli atambadili mnyama kwa mnyama, ndipo yeye na badala yake watakuwa watakatifu.
sw.B: Mwenye mnyama asimbadilishe wala asiweke mwingine mahali pake, mzuri badala ya duni au duni badala ya mzuri. Akimbadilisha mnyama mmoja kwa mwingine, wote wawili, yule wa kwanza na yule aliyewekwa mahali pake, watakuwa watakatifu.
sw.R: Mwenye mnyama asimbadilishe kwa mnyama mwingine, bora kwa duni au duni kwa bora. Akibadilisha, wanyama wote wawili watakuwa mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

ko.L: 그는 그것을 바꾸지 말고, 그것을 맞바꾸지도 말라. 좋은 것을 나쁜 것으로, 나쁜 것을 좋은 것으로 [바꾸지 말라]. 만일 그가 정말로 짐승을 짐승으로 맞바꾸면, 그것과 그 대신한 것이 둘 다 거룩할 것이다.
ko.B: 주인은 그것을 다른 짐승으로 바꾸거나 대신하지 말라. 좋은 것을 나쁜 것으로든 나쁜 것을 좋은 것으로든 바꾸어서는 안 된다. 만일 짐승을 다른 짐승으로 바꾸면, 처음 짐승과 그 대신 바친 짐승이 둘 다 거룩하게 된다.
ko.R: 주인은 그 짐승을 다른 짐승과 바꾸면 안 된다. 더 좋은 것을 더 나쁜 것으로든, 더 나쁜 것을 더 좋은 것으로든 바꾸면 안 된다. 만일 바꾸면, 두 짐승이 모두 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 것이 된다.

decisions.choice: replace ... exchange: no substitute of any kind
decisions.reason: Two verbs are used, both meaning to put one thing in place of another. Together they rule out any swap, whether to the giver's loss or gain. The second verb returns in verse 33 for the tithe of animals.

decisions.choice: it and its substitute will be holy: the attempt costs the owner both
decisions.reason: Whoever tries to exchange a vowed animal loses both: the first stays holy and the second becomes holy as well.

decisions.choice: will belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains "holy" here as belonging to the LORD, the sense of m2 in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "바꾸다" and "맞바꾸다" / "대신하다" for the two Hebrew verbs
decisions.reason: Korean keeps two verbs so that no kind of substitute is left open, as the meaning decision says.

source.text: וְאִם֙ כָּל־בְּהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱמִ֥יד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And if any animal unclean which not people bring near of it [as] an offering to Yahweh, and he will station the animal before the priest,

en.L: And if [it is] any unclean animal, of which [people] do not bring near an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then he shall set the animal before the priest,
en.B: If the vow is of an unclean animal, of the kind that may not be presented as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the animal is to be brought before the priest,
en.R: Someone may promise an unclean animal, one that cannot be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the animal must be brought to the priest.

es.L: Y si [es] cualquier animal impuro, del que no [se] presenta ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, entonces pondrá el animal delante del sacerdote,
es.B: Si el voto es de un animal impuro, de los que no se pueden presentar como ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el animal será presentado ante el sacerdote,
es.R: Alguien puede prometer un animal impuro, uno que no se puede ofrecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Entonces el animal tiene que ser llevado al sacerdote.

fr.L: Et si [c’est] un animal impur quelconque, dont [on] ne fait pas approcher d’offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, alors il placera l’animal devant le prêtre,
fr.B: Si le vœu porte sur un animal impur, de ceux qu’on ne peut pas présenter en offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, l’animal sera présenté au prêtre,
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut promettre un animal impur, qu’on ne peut pas offrir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Alors l’animal doit être amené au prêtre.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [ni] mnyama yeyote aliye najisi, ambaye [watu] hawamsogezi kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ndipo atamsimamisha mnyama huyo mbele ya kuhani,
sw.B: Ikiwa nadhiri ni ya mnyama aliye najisi, wa aina isiyoweza kutolewa kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mnyama huyo ataletwa mbele ya kuhani,
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kuahidi mnyama aliye najisi, ambaye hawezi kutolewa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hapo lazima mnyama huyo aletwe kwa kuhani.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 [그것이] 사람들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 가까이 바치지 않는 부정한 짐승이면, 그는 그 짐승을 제사장 앞에 세워야 한다.
ko.B: 서원한 것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 바칠 수 없는 부정한 짐승이면, 그 짐승을 제사장 앞에 데려가야 한다.
ko.R: 누가 부정한 짐승, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물로 바칠 수 없는 짐승을 바치겠다고 약속할 수 있다. 그러면 그 짐승을 제사장에게 데려가야 한다.

decisions.choice: unclean animal: one not allowed on the altar
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means an animal that may not be sacrificed, such as a donkey or a camel (11:4; Exodus 13:13). It could still be vowed, and its value was given to the sanctuary instead (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: "부정한" for unclean
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for ritual uncleanness; "더러운" would suggest dirt.

source.text: וְהֶעֱרִ֤יךְ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹתָ֔הּ בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and will value the priest it, between good and between bad; according to your valuation, the priest, so it will be.

en.L: and the priest shall value it, whether good or bad; according to your valuation, O priest, so it shall be.
en.B: and the priest will set its value according to whether it is good or poor. The value he sets will stand.
en.R: The priest will decide how much it is worth, whether it is a good animal or a poor one. The price the priest sets is final.

es.L: y el sacerdote lo valorará, sea bueno o malo; conforme a tu valoración, oh sacerdote, así será.
es.B: y el sacerdote fijará su valor según sea bueno o malo. El valor que él fije se mantendrá.
es.R: El sacerdote decidirá cuánto vale, sea un animal bueno o uno malo. El precio que fije el sacerdote es definitivo.

fr.L: et le prêtre l’estimera, qu’il soit bon ou mauvais ; selon ton estimation, ô prêtre, ainsi il en sera.
fr.B: et le prêtre fixera sa valeur selon qu’il est bon ou médiocre. La valeur qu’il fixera sera maintenue.
fr.R: Le prêtre décidera combien il vaut, que ce soit un bon animal ou un animal médiocre. Le prix que le prêtre fixe est définitif.

sw.L: naye kuhani atamkadiria thamani, akiwa mzuri au mbaya; kama makadirio yako, ee kuhani, ndivyo itakavyokuwa.
sw.B: naye kuhani atakadiria thamani yake kulingana na kama ni mzuri au duni. Thamani atakayoweka itasimama.
sw.R: Kuhani ataamua thamani yake, akiwa mnyama mzuri au duni. Bei atakayoweka kuhani haibadiliki.

ko.L: 그러면 제사장은 그것이 좋든 나쁘든 그 값을 매길 것이다. 제사장이여, 네가 매기는 값대로 그것이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 제사장은 그 짐승이 좋은지 나쁜지에 따라 값을 매긴다. 제사장이 매긴 값이 그대로 정해진다.
ko.R: 제사장은 그 짐승이 좋은지 나쁜지 보고 값을 정할 것이다. 제사장이 정한 값은 바꿀 수 없다.

decisions.choice: according to your valuation, priest: the priest's value is final
decisions.reason: The fixed word "your valuation" (verse 2) here stands next to "the priest", and may be read as addressed to him ("your valuation, O priest") or as "the valuation of the priest". Either way, the value the priest sets is the one that holds.

decisions.choice: between good and bad: whatever its quality
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole range from best to worst; the priest values the animal as it is, as in verse 14 for a house.

decisions.choice: O priest
decisions.reason: Literal shows the most direct reading of the Hebrew, where "your valuation" is followed by "the priest"; see m1.

decisions.choice: "제사장이여, 네가 매기는 값대로" keeps the Hebrew turn to the priest at Literal
decisions.reason: The English Literal reads the phrase as an address to the priest; Korean keeps it with the vocative "-이여".

source.text: וְאִם־גָּאֹ֖ל יִגְאָלֶ֑נָּה וְיָסַ֥ף חֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ עַל־עֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed he redeems it, and he will add its fifth to your valuation.

en.L: And if he does indeed redeem it, then he shall add its fifth to your valuation.
en.B: If the owner does redeem it, they must pay the valuation and a fifth more.
en.R: If the owner wants to buy the animal back, they must pay the set price plus one fifth more.

es.L: Y si de hecho lo rescata, entonces añadirá su quinta parte a tu valoración.
es.B: Si el dueño llega a rescatarlo, tendrá que pagar la valoración y una quinta parte más.
es.R: Si el dueño quiere volver a comprar el animal, tiene que pagar el precio fijado y una quinta parte más.

fr.L: Et s’il le rachète vraiment, alors il ajoutera son cinquième à ton estimation.
fr.B: Si le propriétaire veut le racheter, il devra payer l’estimation et un cinquième en plus.
fr.R: Si le propriétaire veut reprendre l’animal en le payant, il doit payer le prix fixé et un cinquième en plus.

sw.L: Na kama kweli atamkomboa, ndipo ataongeza sehemu yake ya tano juu ya makadirio yako.
sw.B: Mwenye mnyama akitaka kumkomboa, atalipa thamani yake na kuongeza sehemu ya tano.
sw.R: Mwenye mnyama akitaka kumnunua tena, lazima alipe bei iliyowekwa na kuongeza sehemu ya tano zaidi.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 그가 정말로 그것을 무르려면, 네가 매기는 값에 그 오분의 일을 더해야 한다.
ko.B: 주인이 그 짐승을 무르려면, 매긴 값에 오분의 일을 더 얹어서 내야 한다.
ko.R: 주인이 그 짐승을 다시 사고 싶으면, 정해진 값에 오분의 일을 더 내야 한다.

decisions.choice: redeem: buy back what was given
decisions.reason: To redeem is to buy back something that has passed to another, as family land is redeemed in 25:25. The owner may take back the unclean animal by paying its value to the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: add its fifth: pay twenty percent above the value
decisions.reason: The added fifth is the same as in the guilt offering (5:16, 24) and the redeemed tithe (verse 31). It makes redeeming a vowed gift costlier than leaving it with the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: buy back
decisions.reason: Readable says "buy back" for "redeem" through this chapter.

decisions.choice: "rescatar" (L, B); "volver a comprar" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter, as "redeem" in Exodus 13 and 21: "rescatar" is the ordinary Spanish for buying back what has passed to another. Readable says plainly "volver a comprar", as the English "buy back".

decisions.choice: "reprendre en le payant" here; "racheter" elsewhere at Readable
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "racheter", as Exodus 13 and 21. At its first use in the chapter Readable spells out what buying back means; later verses say "racheter", which is ordinary French for it.

decisions.choice: "kukomboa" (L, B); "kununua tena" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter, as "redeem" in Exodus 13 and 21. Readable says "kununua tena" (buy again), as the English "buy back".

decisions.choice: "무르다" (Literal, Balanced), "다시 사다" (Readable) for redeeming what was vowed
decisions.reason: As in chapter 25: "무르다" is the Korean verb for taking back by paying the price; Readable uses the plainer "다시 사다".

source.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־יַקְדִּ֨שׁ אֶת־בֵּית֥וֹ קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲרִ֥יךְ אֹת֛וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יָקֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man, when he consecrates his house [as] holy to Yahweh, and will value it the priest between good and between bad; as will value it the priest, so it will stand.

en.L: And {{gender:a person|a man}}, when he consecrates his house [as] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then the priest shall value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall stand.
en.B: When {{gender:anyone|any man}} consecrates a house as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priest is to judge whether it is in good or poor condition and set its value. The value the priest sets will stand.
en.R: Someone may set apart their house as holy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the priest will decide how much it is worth, whether it is a good house or a poor one. The price he sets will not change.

es.L: Y cuando alguien consagre su casa [como cosa] santa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el sacerdote la valorará, sea buena o mala; como la valore el sacerdote, así quedará.
es.B: Cuando alguien consagre una casa como cosa santa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el sacerdote juzgará si está en buen o mal estado y fijará su valor. El valor que fije el sacerdote se mantendrá.
es.R: Alguien puede apartar su casa como santa para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Entonces el sacerdote decidirá cuánto vale, sea una casa buena o una mala. El precio que él fije no cambiará.

fr.L: Et quand quelqu’un consacrera sa maison [comme chose] sainte {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, le prêtre l’estimera, qu’elle soit bonne ou mauvaise ; comme le prêtre l’estimera, ainsi elle sera maintenue.
fr.B: Lorsque quelqu’un consacre une maison comme chose sainte {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, le prêtre jugera si elle est en bon ou en mauvais état et en fixera la valeur. La valeur que fixera le prêtre sera maintenue.
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut mettre à part sa maison comme sainte pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Alors le prêtre décidera combien elle vaut, que ce soit une bonne maison ou une maison en mauvais état. Le prix qu’il fixe ne changera pas.

sw.L: Na mtu atakapoitakasa nyumba yake [iwe] takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ndipo kuhani ataikadiria thamani, ikiwa nzuri au mbaya; kama kuhani atakavyoikadiria, ndivyo itakavyosimama.
sw.B: Mtu akiitakasa nyumba kuwa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kuhani ataamua kama iko katika hali nzuri au duni na kukadiria thamani yake. Thamani atakayoweka kuhani itasimama.
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kuitenga nyumba yake kuwa takatifu kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hapo kuhani ataamua thamani yake, ikiwa ni nyumba nzuri au duni. Bei atakayoweka haitabadilika.

ko.L: 그리고 누구든지 자기 집을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩하게 구별하여 바치면, 제사장은 그것이 좋든 나쁘든 그 값을 매길 것이다. 제사장이 매기는 대로 그대로 정해질 것이다.
ko.B: 누구든지 자기 집을 거룩하게 구별하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바치면, 제사장은 그 집이 좋은지 나쁜지 살펴 값을 매겨야 한다. 제사장이 매긴 값이 그대로 정해진다.
ko.R: 누가 자기 집을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩한 것으로 바칠 수 있다. 그러면 제사장은 그 집이 좋은지 나쁜지 보고 값을 정할 것이다. 제사장이 정한 값은 바뀌지 않는다.

decisions.choice: consecrates as holy: gives over to the LORD
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to make holy, here to hand property over to the LORD as a gift to the sanctuary, as in 8:10. The house would then belong to the sanctuary, or the owner could redeem it (verse 15).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone who owns a house
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the law is for any owner, man or woman.

decisions.choice: a house / their house
decisions.reason: Balanced avoids the pronoun with "a house"; Readable uses "their" for the owner, who may be a man or a woman. Literal keeps "his".

decisions.choice: "거룩하게 구별하여 바치다" for consecrating
decisions.reason: The phrase says what consecrating means, setting something apart as God's; "성별하다" is an older church word few readers know.

source.text: וְאִ֨ם־הַמַּקְדִּ֔ישׁ יִגְאַ֖ל אֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ וְ֠יָסַף חֲמִישִׁ֧ית כֶּֽסֶף־עֶרְכְּךָ֛ עָלָ֖יו וְהָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if the one consecrating will redeem his house, and he will add a fifth of [the] silver of your valuation to it, and it will be his.

en.L: And if the one who consecrated [it] redeems his house, then he shall add a fifth of the silver of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.
en.B: If the one who consecrated the house wants to redeem it, they must pay its value in silver and a fifth more, and it will be theirs again.
en.R: If the owner wants to buy the house back, they must pay the set price plus one fifth more. Then it will be theirs again.

es.L: Y si el que [la] consagró rescata su casa, entonces añadirá la quinta parte de la plata de tu valoración, y será suya.
es.B: Si el que consagró la casa quiere rescatarla, tendrá que pagar su valor en plata y una quinta parte más, y volverá a ser suya.
es.R: Si el dueño quiere volver a comprar la casa, tiene que pagar el precio fijado y una quinta parte más. Entonces volverá a ser suya.

fr.L: Et si celui qui [l’]a consacrée rachète sa maison, alors il ajoutera le cinquième de l’argent de ton estimation, et elle sera à lui.
fr.B: Si celui qui a consacré la maison veut la racheter, il devra payer sa valeur en argent et un cinquième en plus, et elle sera de nouveau à lui.
fr.R: Si le propriétaire veut racheter la maison, il doit payer le prix fixé et un cinquième en plus. Alors elle sera de nouveau à lui.

sw.L: Na ikiwa yule aliyeitakasa ataikomboa nyumba yake, ndipo ataongeza sehemu ya tano ya fedha ya makadirio yako juu yake, nayo itakuwa yake.
sw.B: Ikiwa aliyeitakasa nyumba anataka kuikomboa, atalipa thamani yake kwa fedha na kuongeza sehemu ya tano, nayo itakuwa yake tena.
sw.R: Mwenye nyumba akitaka kuinunua tena, lazima alipe bei iliyowekwa na kuongeza sehemu ya tano zaidi. Ndipo itakuwa yake tena.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 그것을 거룩하게 구별하여 바친 자가 자기 집을 무르려면, 네가 매기는 값의 은에 오분의 일을 더해야 하고, 그러면 그것이 그의 것이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 집을 바친 사람이 그 집을 무르려면, 매긴 값의 은에 오분의 일을 더 얹어서 내야 한다. 그러면 그 집은 다시 그의 것이 된다.
ko.R: 주인이 그 집을 다시 사고 싶으면, 정해진 값에 오분의 일을 더 내야 한다. 그러면 그 집은 다시 그의 것이 된다.

decisions.choice: add a fifth of the silver: pay the value plus twenty percent
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, the one who redeems pays the value set by the priest and adds a fifth. "Silver" is the payment, weighed out (verse 3).

decisions.choice: theirs again
decisions.reason: "It will be his" means the house returns to its owner; Balanced and Readable add "again".

source.text: וְאִ֣ם׀מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֗וֹ יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה עֶרְכְּךָ֖ לְפִ֣י זַרְע֑וֹ זֶ֚רַע חֹ֣מֶר שְׂעֹרִ֔ים בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And if some of [the] field of his possession a man consecrates to Yahweh, and will be your valuation according to the mouth of its seed: seed of a homer of barley for fifty shekel[s] of silver.

en.L: And if {{gender:a person|a man}} consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} some of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to its seed: seed of a homer of barley at fifty shekels of silver.
en.B: If {{gender:anyone|any man}} consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} part of a field that is their family's land, its value will follow the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for {{units:about 6 bushels|a homer}} of barley seed.
en.R: Someone may give part of their family's land to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the price will depend on how much seed it takes to plant it. The price is fifty shekels of silver for every {{units:about 6 bushels|a homer}} of barley seed.

es.L: Y si alguien consagra {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} parte del campo de su posesión, entonces tu valoración será conforme a su semilla: la semilla de un homer de cebada a cincuenta siclos de plata.
es.B: Si alguien consagra {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} parte de un campo que es tierra de su familia, su valor dependerá de la semilla necesaria para sembrarlo: cincuenta siclos de plata por {{units:unos 220 litros|un homer}} de semilla de cebada.
es.R: Alguien puede dar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} parte de la tierra de su familia. Entonces el precio dependerá de cuánta semilla hace falta para sembrarla. El precio es de cincuenta siclos de plata por {{units:unos 220 litros|un homer}} de semilla de cebada.

fr.L: Et si quelqu’un consacre {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} une partie du champ de sa possession, alors ton estimation sera selon sa semence : la semence d’un homer d’orge à cinquante sicles d’argent.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un consacre {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} une partie d’un champ qui est la terre de sa famille, sa valeur sera fixée d’après la semence qu’il faut pour l’ensemencer : cinquante sicles d’argent pour {{units:environ 220 litres|un homer}} de semence d’orge.
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut donner {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} une partie de la terre de sa famille. Alors le prix dépendra de la quantité de semence qu’il faut pour la semer. Le prix est de cinquante sicles d’argent pour {{units:environ 220 litres|un homer}} de semence d’orge.

sw.L: Na ikiwa mtu atamtakasia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sehemu ya shamba la milki yake, ndipo makadirio yako yatakuwa kulingana na mbegu zake: mbegu za homeri moja ya shayiri kwa shekeli hamsini za fedha.
sw.B: Mtu akimtakasia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sehemu ya shamba lililo ardhi ya urithi wa jamaa yake, thamani yake itafuata kiasi cha mbegu kinachohitajika kulipanda: shekeli hamsini za fedha kwa mbegu za shayiri {{units:kama lita 220|homeri moja}}.
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kumpa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sehemu ya ardhi ya jamaa yake. Hapo bei itategemea kiasi cha mbegu kinachohitajika kuipanda. Bei ni shekeli hamsini za fedha kwa mbegu za shayiri {{units:kama lita 220|homeri moja}}.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 누가 자기 소유지의 밭 얼마를 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩하게 구별하여 바치면, 네가 매기는 값은 그 씨앗에 따라 정해질 것이다. 보리 씨 한 호멜에 은 오십 세겔이다.
ko.B: 누구든지 집안 대대로 내려온 밭 가운데 얼마를 거룩하게 구별하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바치면, 그 값은 거기에 뿌릴 씨앗의 양에 따라 정한다. 보리 씨 {{units:220리터쯤|한 호멜}}에 은 오십 세겔이다.
ko.R: 누가 자기 집안의 땅 가운데 얼마를 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바칠 수 있다. 그러면 그 값은 그 땅에 씨를 뿌리는 데 드는 씨앗의 양에 따라 정한다. 보리 씨 {{units:220리터쯤|한 호멜}}마다 은 오십 세겔이다.

decisions.choice: the field of his possession: inherited family land
decisions.reason: "Possession" is land held as a family's lasting share, which could not be sold for good and returned to the family in the Jubilee (25:10, 23-28). The field given here is that kind of land; a bought field is treated in verses 22-24.

decisions.choice: homer: the largest dry measure
decisions.reason: A homer was a dry measure, about 6 bushels (roughly 220 liters), perhaps first the load a donkey could carry. It was ten ephahs (Ezekiel 45:11).

decisions.choice: according to its seed: by the amount of seed needed to sow it
decisions.reason: The field is valued by its size, measured by the seed it takes to sow it: fifty shekels for each homer of seed. Verses 17-18 show that this is the price for the full fifty years between Jubilees, about a shekel a year. The phrase could instead mean the harvest the field yields, but "seed of a homer" points to sowing.

decisions.choice: family's land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his possession" is: the land a family holds by inheritance (m1).

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 220 litros|un homer}}
decisions.reason: Where the English converts the homer to US bushels, Spanish converts to metric (about 220 litres, m2), with the original unit as the alternative, as the terms list sets for the Pentateuch. Literal keeps "un homer", as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 220 litres|un homer}}
decisions.reason: Where the English converts the homer to US bushels, French converts to metric (about 220 litres, m2), with the original unit as the alternative, as the terms list sets for the Pentateuch. Literal keeps "un homer", as the English does.
